info.title: yonyon.ai public API
info.description:
Public, unauthenticated endpoints an AI agent can call on yonyon.ai. No API key, OAuth, or client registration. The only constraint is rate: 10 requests per IP per minute. Versioning: this is major version 1, sent as an `X-API-Version: 1` response header on every endpoint. Deprecation policy: breaking changes ship as a new major version; a version scheduled for removal is announced in advance via `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response headers (RFC 9745 / RFC 8594) and stays available for at least 6 months after its successor is announced. Full policy: https://yonyon.ai/api-deprecation.md.

Idempotency: every endpoint is read-only, so all operations are naturally idempotent. POST /ask and POST /api/v1/batch accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` request header (maximum 128 characters) and echo it back on the response as an `Idempotency-Key` response header, so a retrying agent can confirm the key was honored and correlate the response with its original request.

Pagination: GET /api/v1/projects uses cursor-based pagination. Pass `limit` (1-50) and `cursor` query parameters. Responses carry `count`, `total`, `nextCursor`, `next_cursor`, and `has_more`. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Never construct a cursor by hand.

Unmatched /api/* paths return this Error envelope with code=not_found (HTTP 404).

servers.description: Production. The public API is read-only and anonymous.
Sandbox (read-only public API; no production side effects). Same origin; see /sandbox.md.

get.description: Machine-readable index of the live public API surface: every endpoint with its method, the enforced rate limit, and pointers at this spec, the RFC 9727 api catalog, and the auth documentation. Public, anonymous, CORS-open, and rate-limited through the same limiter as every other endpoint, so the response carries live `RateLimit-*` and `X-RateLimit-*` values rather than only documenting them. Also sends `Link: <https://yonyon.ai/.well-known/api-catalog>; rel="api-catalog"` (RFC 9727). No authentication is required or accepted: this path always answers 200 and never sends a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. See https://yonyon.ai/auth.md.

post.summary: Ask a question about Yonatan Gross (streaming)
post.description: Streams a grounded answer about Yonatan's work, projects, services, and experience. Public and rate-limited (10 requests/IP/minute). No authentication required. Browser-facing: requests must carry an Origin matching the host (CSRF). For server-side agents, prefer POST /ask.

200.description: A streamed plain-text answer (concatenate the chunks).

text/plain.example: Yonatan builds production AI systems end to end.

403.description: CSRF rejected (Origin missing or not allowed).

post.description: Microsoft NLWeb endpoint. Agent-facing single-shot query over the same RAG + model that powers the site chat. No Origin/CSRF requirement. Returns JSON with `_meta` { response_type, version } by default; returns Server-Sent Events (start / result / complete) when the caller sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, `?streaming=true`, or `{ "prefer": { "streaming": true } }`. Rate-limited (10 requests/IP/minute). Accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key` request header, echoed on the response.

200.description: JSON answer (default) or text/event-stream when streaming is requested.

get.description: Returns a small JSON descriptor of how to call POST /ask. Fetch this first if you are discovering the endpoint programmatically. Also accepts ?query= for a GET query and ?streaming=true to request SSE.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Natural-language question. Same as the POST body field `query`.

parameters.name: streaming
parameters.description: If true, respond with text/event-stream instead of JSON.

example.answer: NLWeb natural-language query endpoint for yonyon.ai. POST {"query":"..."} (or GET /ask?query=) to ask about Yonatan Gross's work, projects, and services. Add Accept: text/event-stream, ?streaming=true, or {"prefer":{"streaming":true}} for SSE (start/result/complete events). Public, no auth, rate-limited (10 req/IP/min).

get.description: Returns Yonatan Gross's portfolio projects as JSON. Public, anonymous, CORS-open, rate-limited (10 requests/IP/minute). Supports an optional `?q=` keyword filter (matched against project name + description) and opaque cursor pagination via `?limit=` (1-50) and `?cursor=`. The response carries `count`, `total`, `nextCursor`, `next_cursor`, and `has_more` (`nextCursor` is null on the last page).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive keyword filter matched against project name and description.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return in this page (integer, 1-50). Omit to return the full list.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque base64url cursor returned as next_cursor by a previous response. Do not construct by hand.

post.summary: Run up to 10 read operations in one request
post.description: Runs up to 10 read-only operations in a single round-trip. Each operation is `{ "op": "projects"|"services"|"about", "params": { "q"?: string } }`; only `projects` uses `q` (a keyword filter). Every operation is read-only and idempotent, so an optional `Idempotency-Key` request header is accepted and echoed on the response. A per-operation failure (e.g. an unknown op) is reported inline with `status: "error"` and never fails the whole batch. Public, anonymous, CORS-open, rate-limited (10 requests/IP/minute).

Accepts a read operation and returns 202 Accepted with a Location header and a job_id in the body. Poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{jobId} for the result. The public API is read-only, so the job always succeeds or fails on the poll; there is no queue to cancel.

q.description: Keyword filter (only applied to the projects op).

202.description: Job accepted. Follow Location or status_url.

get.description: Returns the result of a job started by POST /api/v1/jobs. The job_id is an opaque token from the 202 body.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: Job identifier returned as job_id by POST /api/v1/jobs.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional client-supplied key (maximum 128 characters) echoed back as an `Idempotency-Key` response header. Every operation on this API is read-only and naturally idempotent; the echo lets a retrying agent correlate responses.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of items to return in this page (integer, 1-50). Omit to return the full list.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque base64url cursor returned as `nextCursor` by a previous response. Do not construct by hand.

X-API-Version.description: Major version of the API serving this response. Currently always "1".

Idempotency-Key.description: Echo of the client-supplied `Idempotency-Key` request header (present only when the request sent one). Truncated to 128 characters.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Present only if this version is deprecated: an IMF-fixdate (or the token "true") marking when deprecation took effect.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only if this version is scheduled for removal: the IMF-fixdate after which it will stop responding.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Epoch seconds when the current window resets.

RateLimit-Limit.description: RFC draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers. Requests allowed per window.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: RFC draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers. Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimit-Reset.description: RFC draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers. Seconds (a delta, not an epoch) until the current window resets.

Link.description: RFC 8288 web links. The API root sends the RFC 9727 `api-catalog` relation pointing at https://yonyon.ai/.well-known/api-catalog. List endpoints send rel="next" when another page is available.

Location.description: URI of the newly accepted job (GET /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}).

count.description: Number of projects in this page.

total.description: Total projects across all pages for the current filter.

nextCursor.description: Opaque base64url cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

next_cursor.description: Snake_case alias of nextCursor, for agents that look up next_cursor.

has_more.description: True when another page is available. Equivalent to next_cursor != null.

operations.description: Between 1 and 10 read operations, executed in order.

q.description: Keyword filter (only applied to the `projects` op).

op.description: The op that ran (or "(missing)" when none was supplied).

status.description: Per-operation outcome. An error here does not fail the batch.

data.description: The op's result payload (shape depends on op), or an { error, code } envelope when status is "error".

Error.description: Typed error envelope returned for every non-2xx response.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (present on rate_limited).

Endpoint.description: One endpoint that is live on this API today.

RateLimitPolicy.description: The rate limit actually enforced on this API, as machine-readable JSON.

scope.description: What the window is keyed on.

ApiRoot.description: Index of the live public API surface, served at GET /api.

version.description: Current major version of the REST surface.

auth.description: Always describes anonymous access. No credential is issued or accepted anywhere on this site.

ApiVersionRoot.description: Index of one major version of the REST surface, served at GET /api/v1.

status.description: Lifecycle of this version. `stable` until a Deprecation/Sunset header says otherwise.

AskDescriptor.title: AskDescriptor
AskDescriptor.description: Self-describing descriptor for the NLWeb query endpoint. Returned by GET /ask so an agent can learn how to call POST /ask without reading prose documentation.

query.description: Always empty on the descriptor; present so the descriptor and a real answer share one shape.

answer.description: Human and agent readable instructions for calling this endpoint.

method.description: HTTP method to use for a real query.

url.description: Absolute URL to POST a query to.

streaming.description: Whether the endpoint can stream Server-Sent Events.

AskStreamStart.title: AskStreamStart
AskStreamStart.description: Payload of the `start` event. Echoes the accepted query.

query.description: The query as the server parsed it.

AskStreamResult.title: AskStreamResult
AskStreamResult.description: Payload of a `result` event. Emitted repeatedly; concatenate `content` across every result event in order to rebuild the full answer.

content.description: One chunk of the answer text.

AskStreamComplete.title: AskStreamComplete
AskStreamComplete.description: Payload of the terminal `complete` event. No further events follow.

AskStreamEvent.title: AskStreamEvent
AskStreamEvent.description: The JSON object carried in the `data:` field of one Server-Sent Event. The SSE `event:` field names which variant it is: `start`, `result`, or `complete`.

ChatStreamText.title: ChatStreamText
ChatStreamText.description: The answer, streamed as plain UTF-8 text chunks over a single response body. There is no framing: concatenate the chunks in arrival order to get the complete answer. The stream ends when the body closes.
examples: Yonatan builds production AI systems end to end.

job_id.description: Opaque job identifier. Pass it to GET /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}.

status_url.description: Absolute URL to poll for the result.

status.description: Jobs on this API complete on the first poll.

result.description: The read result (projects list, services markdown, or about markdown).

BadRequest.description: Malformed request (invalid JSON, validation failure, or blocked content).

Unavailable.description: The assistant is temporarily unavailable (model backend not configured/reachable).
